compliance.emc: FCC 47 CFR Part 15; ICES-003 / ICES-GEN; BS EN 55032; BS EN 55035; EN 300 386; CISPR 32; CISPR 35; IEC/EN 61000 series; AS/NZS CISPR 32; VCCI-CISPR 32; BSMI CNS 15936; KS C 9835; KS C 9832 (datasheet Table 6)
compliance.substances: RoHS; TSCA; POPs; WEEE; California Prop 65; REACH (datasheet Table 6)

environmental.altitude: no performance degradation to 1829 m (6000 ft) at 0 to 40 C (guide, Environmental Specifications; datasheet Table 3, AFI with 400G ZR optics is limited to sea level at 40 C)
environmental.humidity: 5 to 90 percent noncondensing, operating and non-operating
environmental.operating-temp: 0 to 40 C (32 to 104 F), for AFO and for AFI (guide Table 30, datasheet Table 3)
environmental.storage-temp: -40 to 70 C (-40 to 158 F) in the shipping container

features.macsec: QFX5130-48CM only, with the S-QFX5KC3-MACSEC-X licence: 32 x 100G SFP56-DD and 4 x 400G QSFP-DD ports support MACsec, up to 9.6 Tbps bidirectional (guide, product overview)
features.optics-qsfp-dd: 400 GbE QSFP-DD optics on ports 48 to 55; breakout cables for 100/25/10 GbE (datasheet)
features.optics-sfp-dd: 100 GbE SFP56-DD cables and 400 GbE AOCs on ports 0 to 47 (guide, Network Ports for QFX5130-48C)
features.optics-sfp-plus: ports 56 and 57 take 10 GbE modules only, on the rear management panel

management.oob: one RJ-45 management port with link and status lamps

performance.breakout-ports: 16 x 200 GbE + 48 x 100/50/25/10 GbE + 2 x 10 GbE, or 72 x 100/50/25/10 GbE + 2 x 10 GbE, or 74 x 10 GbE (datasheet Table 2)
performance.network-port-speeds: ports 0 to 47 default to 100 GbE with SFP56-DD optics; ports 48 to 55 default to 400 GbE with QSFP-DD optics (guide, Setting Port Speed and Channelization)
performance.throughput: up to 8 Tbps unidirectional and 16 Tbps bidirectional (datasheet Table 2)

physical.weight-note: 27 lb (12.24 kg) with power supplies and fans installed (guide Table 31)

platform.software: Junos OS Evolved, first release 23.4R1-S1-EVO for the QFX5130-48C and 23.4R2-S1-EVO for the QFX5130-48CM
platform.storage: two internal 100 GB SSDs (datasheet Table 2); the guide's RMA procedure describes two SSDs

power.power-input-ac: 100 to 127 VAC and 200 to 240 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz; 12 A at 100 to 127 VAC, 9 A at 200 to 240 VAC (guide Table 20)
power.power-input-dc: rated -48 to -60 VDC, operating -40 to -72 VDC, 40 A maximum (guide Table 27)
power.power-measurement-note: Maximum at 40 C ambient with SR optics at 100 percent load with IMIX traffic; typical at 25 C with DACs at 50 percent load with IMIX traffic, excluding transceivers (datasheet Table 4)
power.redundancy-note: two supplies, 1+1, each able to carry the whole switch; both should be installed, on feeds A and B

thermal.airflow-note: AFO is front-to-back (port-to-FRU); AFI is back-to-front (FRU-to-port); no mixing of fans and supplies of different direction
thermal.fans: six fan modules, redundant at the rotor level; the switch runs 240 seconds without thermal shutdown while one is replaced

ac-b2f.description: QFX5130-48C-AFI: two 1600 W AC supplies (JPSU-1600W-1UACAFI) and six back-to-front fan modules (QFX5130-48C-FANAI). All have a Juniper azure blue handle and the label AIR IN (guide Tables 4 and 17).

ac-f2b.description: QFX5130-48C-AFO: two 1600 W AC supplies (JPSU-1600W-1UACAFO) and six front-to-back fan modules (QFX5130-48C-FANAO). All have a Juniper gold handle and the label AIR OUT (guide Tables 4 and 17).

chas.description: QFX5130-48C-CHAS, the spare chassis, shipped without power supplies or fan modules. Either AC or DC supplies and AIR OUT or AIR IN fan modules are ordered separately, and supplies and fans of one airflow only go in. The supply and fan bays are shown open.

cm-ac-b2f.description: QFX5130-48CM-AFI, the MACsec-capable model: two 1600 W AC supplies (JPSU-1600W-1UACAFI) and six back-to-front fan modules (QFX5130-48C-FANAI). The panel is the QFX5130-48C's.

cm-ac-f2b.description: QFX5130-48CM-AFO, the MACsec-capable model: two 1600 W AC supplies (JPSU-1600W-1UACAFO) and six front-to-back fan modules (QFX5130-48C-FANAO). The panel is the QFX5130-48C's. MACsec needs the S-QFX5KC3-MACSEC-X licence.

cm-chas.description: QFX5130-48CM-CHAS, the spare chassis of the MACsec-capable model, shipped without power supplies or fan modules. The supply and fan bays are shown open.

cm-dc-b2f.description: QFX5130-48CM-D-AFI, the MACsec-capable model: two 1600 W DC supplies (JPSU-1600W-1UDCAFI) and six back-to-front fan modules. The panel is the QFX5130-48C's.

cm-dc-f2b.description: QFX5130-48CM-D-AFO, the MACsec-capable model: two 1600 W DC supplies (JPSU-1600W-1UDCAFO) and six front-to-back fan modules. The panel is the QFX5130-48C's.

dc-b2f.description: QFX5130-48C-D-AFI: two 1600 W DC supplies (JPSU-1600W-1UDCAFI) and six back-to-front fan modules. Each supply has a single feed, so feeds A and B go one to each.

dc-f2b.description: QFX5130-48C-D-AFO: two 1600 W DC supplies (JPSU-1600W-1UDCAFO) and six front-to-back fan modules. Each supply has a single feed, so feeds A and B go one to each.

datasheet.title: QFX5130 Line of Switches Datasheet (Juniper Networks, 1000680-018-EN, July 2025)

description: Juniper QFX5130-48C, a 1RU data-centre leaf switch running Junos OS Evolved, with 48 SFP56-DD ports (100 GbE) for servers and 8 QSFP-DD uplink ports (400 GbE). The port side carries the 48 SFP56-DD cages in two rows of 24, in three groups of eight columns, and the eight uplinks in two rows of four, with a lamp for each. The fan and supply side carries the management panel at the left end: the RJ-45 management and console ports, a USB port, the reset button, the three chassis lamps, the 10 MHz and 1 PPS output connectors, two SFP+ ports and the ESD point. Six fan modules and two power supplies fill the rest of that side. The QFX5130-48CM has the same panel and is MACsec capable, so it is a set of configurations of this device. Both ship in four power and airflow variants, AC or DC supplies with front-to-back (AIR OUT) or back-to-front (AIR IN) airflow, and as a spare chassis with no supplies and no fan modules.

gaps.wanted: The depth of the fan module and of the power supplies. The guide's figures are isometric and carry no scale and its tables state weights only for the whole chassis.

What the windows at the corners of the lower (console) RJ-45 jack are. The guide describes lamps for the management port only (figure 32, Table 16) and none for the console. Not drawn on the console jack.

The part number of the fan modules. The datasheet's ordering table says QFX5130-48C-FANAO and -FANAI; guide Tables 4 and 17 say QFX5130-48C-FANAFO and -FANAFI. The datasheet's spelling is each component's model, since it is the one a buyer orders, and the guide's is in its description.

The airflow of JPSU-1600W-1UDCAFO. Guide Table 24 prints "Airflow In (port-to-FRU)" in one row and "Airflow Out (port-to-FRU)" in the row for the 48C; Table 3 and the part number's AFO say port-to-FRU is Airflow Out (front-to-back). Airflow Out is used.
The lower AC input range. Guide Table 20 and the datasheet's Table 2 both say 100 to 127 VAC for the 48C and 48CM, while the datasheet's 32CD column says 115 to 127 VAC. The 48C figure is carried.

The DC input current. Guide Table 27 and the datasheet's Table 2 say 40 A maximum for the 48C and 48CM, while the 32CD says 35 A. The 40 A figure is carried. The guide's breaker advice reads "40 A (80 VDC) minimum", which is not repeated.
The size of the two SSDs. The datasheet's Table 2 says 2 x 100 GB for the 48C and 48CM; the guide's overview of the 32CD says 2 x 50 GB and its 48C text gives no size. The datasheet's 100 GB is used.

Which 32 of the SFP56-DD ports and which 4 of the QSFP-DD ports support MACsec on the 48CM. The guide says "32x 100G SFP56-DD and 4x 400G QSFP-DD ports support MACsec" and does not number them. Nothing is marked on the ports.

The connector type of the 10M Out and PPS Out jacks. The guide calls them "clock input and output connectors" and does not name a type; the photograph shows gold coaxial jacks 6.5 mm across, drawn as the library's SMA jack. Estimated. Whether each is an input or an output is not stated either; the legends say Out.
The USB revision. The guide names a "USB slot" and no revision, and says a drive up to 16.5 mm wide is needed to reach the reset pinhole. The port is drawn with the kit's neutral usb2 skin.

The lid, the underside and the side walls. The image library's side and top views are perspective photographs with no scale, the guide has no flat figure of them, and its mounting and grounding figures show the brackets and the two protective-earth screws on the top in perspective only.
The protective earthing terminal, two 10-32 screw holes on the top of the chassis near the management panel (guide figure 101). The figure is an isometric with no scale, so no position is given.
The rack ears' positions and the rack kit's contract. The guide names QFX5130-1RU-4PRMK and no kit contract exists in the library; none is written here.
The model name printed on the rear management panel. The 48C photograph prints QFX5130-48C and the 48CM photograph QFX5130-48CM; the two models share this device, so neither name is drawn.

esd.description: the wrist-strap ESD point on the management panel (guide figure 29, callout 1)

attrs.redundancy-note: QFX5130 hardware guide, QFX5130 Component Redundancy: the QFX5130-48C and QFX5130-48CM have six fan modules and support redundancy only at the rotor level; one rotor of a module may fail, and more than one failed rotor can trigger chassis alarms and shutdown

mgmt.mixed: the out-of-band cluster at the left end of the rear - an RJ-45 management port, an RJ-45 console port, a USB port and the recessed reset button. Four kinds, one purpose: reaching and recovering the switch when the data plane cannot.

attrs.redundancy-note: two supplies, each able to carry the whole switch; one may be removed at a time while the switch runs

qsfpdd-400g.description: Ports 48 to 55 as printed, rel-pos carrying the printed number, since the origin token cannot express a block that starts at 48.

qsfpdd-leds.description: One bicolour lamp per QSFP-DD uplink, above the top row (guide Table 10).

sfp-dd-100g.description: Ports 0 to 47, the 100 GbE SFP56-DD cages, three groups of eight columns.

sfp-dd-leds.description: One bicolour lamp per SFP56-DD port, above the top row (guide Table 10).

sfp-plus.description: Ports 56 and 57 as printed, on the rear management panel, rel-pos carrying the printed number, since the origin token cannot express a block that starts at 56.

sfp-plus-leds.description: One bicolour lamp per SFP+ port, above the cages (guide Table 11).

status-leds.description: The three chassis lamps ALM, SYS and ID (guide Table 14).

timing.description: the 10 MHz and 1 PPS clock connectors, a pair of coaxial jacks that carry the switch's timing references

name: qfx5130-48c

chassis.note: guide Table 31 (QFX5130-48C): 1.72 in (4.3 cm) high, 17.28 in (43.9 cm) wide, 20.5 in (52.1 cm) deep, 27 lb (12.24 kg) with power supplies and fans installed, 1RU. The inch figures are used and the centimetre ones in the same cell are rounded copies of them. The datasheet's Table 2 gives the same 17.28 x 1.72 x 20.5 in for the 48C and 48CM. Table 31 has no row of its own for the 48CM; Table 4 and the datasheet group the two. The width is the body, not the brackets. The table does not say whether the depth includes the handles of the supplies and fans.

colour.note: The front plate samples #d6d6d7 (median of a bare patch at the right edge) and the rear management panel #5a6070. The chassis colour is the front's. The rear sheet is drawn as one label-plate decor rect, #4d515a, a little darker than the sample because the photograph is lit from the front; the supplies and fans are components with their own colours. The photographs are lit warmly and these are their values, not a paint reference.

drawing-vs-photo.note: The guide's figure 29 draws the rear in outline, with the fans' hex grille and the supplies as line art, and the photograph agrees on what is where. Figure 29 marks the printed ground sign next to the ESD point as a plain circle with a cross, and the photograph prints the same sign above the ESD point, which is not drawn. Figure 16 and the 48C photograph (1500 px) show the front without lit lamps and figure 18, the 48CM, with some lit. The two fronts carry the same legends and the same metal.

ears-and-kits.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide names the toolless four-post rack mount kit QFX5130-1RU-4PRMK (Mount the QFX5130-48C/QFX5130-48CM Switch by Using the QFX5130-1RU-4PRMK Rack Mount Kit) and the datasheet orders it. The library holds no contract for the kit and none is written here, so `chassis.ears` and `chassis.kits` are left out and a gap says so. The modelled body is the 438.9 mm chassis, without brackets.

front-blue-tab.note: A light-blue tab at the lower left, 21.1 mm wide and 1.9 mm high, at 25.2 mm from the left, stands against the bottom lip. The guide's figure 21 draws it unlabelled. It is the chassis serial number pull-out the QFX5130-32CD's figure 20 labels (callout 7), so it is drawn as decor, because it is a label card and not a part the library models. Estimated.

gate-1.note: Front photograph (48CM, 2100 x 507 px): the body, between its left and right edges, is 1872 px wide and 184 px from the top edge to the bottom lip, an aspect of 10.2 against the table's 438.9 / 43.7 = 10.04 (1.3 percent out). Scale 4.265 px/mm across, used on both axes, with the origin at the body's left edge (x 124.3 px) and top edge (y 165.6 px). Rear photograph (48CM, 2100 x 523 px): the body is 1860 px wide, 4.238 px/mm, origin x 119.5 px and y 154.3 px. The guide's flat figures 21 and 29 were used to read and count; the photographs were measured.

lifecycle.note: Searched for an end-of-life announcement. No Juniper notice was found and the guide, published 2026-10-14, states none; the guide says the 48C is supported from Junos OS 23.4R1-S1-EVO and the 48CM from 23.4R2-S1-EVO. The device states none announced. Estimated, because absence from the pages searched is not a statement by the maker.

logo.note: The maker's logo and its lockup are printed in a label across the top of the management panel, beside the model name, which the photographs print as QFX5130-48CM or QFX5130-48C. The logo is not drawn: a logo-zone region is reserved where it stands. The printed model name is not drawn either: the two models share this one device and one panel, and the name is the only thing that differs between their rears, so no one name is true of both. The front prints neither.

mgmt-panel.note: The management panel is at the left end of the rear, not the front (guide, QFX5130-48C Management Panel Overview and figure 29), 54 mm wide. From the left: the ESD point (callout 1), the 10M Out and PPS Out clock connectors (callout 2), a stacked pair of RJ-45 jacks in one shield 15.8 mm wide, a USB-A port standing on its side, the RESET pinhole, and the ALM, SYS and ID lamps (callouts 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11), then two stacked SFP+ cages (callouts 3 and 6). The legends "MGMT up-arrow" and "down-arrow CON" over the jacks make the upper jack the management port and the lower the console, the reverse of the QFX5130-32CD, and figure 29's callouts 7 and 8 agree. The photograph shows the upper jack's contacts and tabs at the top and the lower one's at the bottom, so the upper is turned 180, as the QFX5130-32CD's stacked pair is.

modules.note: The six fan modules (QFX5130-48C-FANAO and -FANAI in the datasheet, QFX5130-48C-FANAFO and -FANAFI in guide Tables 4 and 17) and the two power supplies (JPSU-1600W-1UACAFO and -AFI, JPSU-1600W-1UDCAFO and -AFI) are field-replaceable units in bays, each its own component. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit that is not a bay: the guide's Table 4 lists the fan modules and supplies as the only replaceable parts. The supplies are the QFX5130-32CD's, reused as they are, because Tables 3 and 4 name the same four part numbers. Each supply carries its own small fan inside (the cooling system is six fan modules and a fan in each supply). The fan lamp is on each fan module.

port-lamps.note: Table 10 gives each SFP-DD and QSFP-DD port one bicolour lamp (green link, green flashing activity, amber blinking fault); the lamps are round windows above the top row, in line with the numerals. For a column of SFP56-DD cages the even port's lamp is at 7.0 mm from the cage block's left edge (measured 7.0, drawn on the cage's centre line at 7.125, the 0.1 mm being inside the reading) and the odd port's at 12.05 mm, with the arrow pair between them at 10.0; the even numeral stands at 4.2 and the odd one at 14.35. For the uplinks the lamps and numerals are lower and wider apart: the even lamp at 2.85 mm and the odd at 15.6 from the column edge, the numerals at 2.9 and 15.8. The lamps are 1.7 mm across, read at 3 times zoom, and estimated to 0.3 mm. Which lamp serves which port is read off figure 21 (each lamp sits beside its own numeral) and is estimated. The 48CM photograph shows lit lamps for some ports (the numerals lit green); that is a state, not a position, and nothing lit is drawn.

port-numbering.note: Printed on the metal above the top row, read off the photograph and figure 21: each column prints "even, lamp, up-arrow down-arrow, lamp, odd" with the even number at the left of its column and the odd one at the right, so the odd number of one column stands next to the even number of the next ("1 2"). The ports run 0 to 47 down each column and left to right, even above odd, and the uplinks 48 to 55 in the same way, with an up-arrow before each even number and a down-arrow after each odd one. Interface names are not printed. The guide names ports 0 to 47 and 48 to 55, and its configuration examples name the interfaces et-0/0/N: after Table 7 (the 48C and 48CM table), "to set port 2 to 100 Gbps" it gives "set interfaces et-0/0/2 speed 100g" and notes "On QFX5130 devices, there is a single FPC and PIC, which is always 0" (Setting Port Speed and Channelization, PDF page 39). So port N is et-0/0/N, as for the QFX5130-32CD; that is recorded here and not in an interfaces block, because the face does not print it.

ports.note: Front photograph: 48 SFP56-DD openings in two rows of 24, in three groups of eight columns, each group a continuous slot with thin webs between its cages. The cages stand on a 60.9 px pitch, 14.28 mm, which is the registry's 14.25 for std/sfp-dd-ganged (TE 114-60027), so the groups are ganged blocks of eight; the groups' centres are 116.7 and 117.0 mm apart (116.85 used), so the gutter is 2.85 mm and the blocks start at 6.5, 123.35 and 240.2 mm. The eight QSFP-DD uplinks stand to the right as four columns of two on the registry's 19.0 mm pitch (18.9 measured), the first column at 357.9 mm. Counts and groups are the guide's figures 16, 18 and 21: callout 1 is the 48 network ports and callout 2 the 8 uplink ports, numbered 0 to 47 and 48 to 55 (the guide's text). The two SFP+ ports are numbered 56 and 57 and are on the rear management panel, not on this face; the guide's text says "We don't see 56 and 57 in the ports panel".

power.note: Table 20 (AC): operating range 100 to 127 VAC and 200 to 240 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz, 12 A at 100 to 127 VAC and 9 A at 200 to 240 VAC, typical 219 W and maximum 609 W. Table 27 (DC): rated -48 to -60 VDC, range -40 to -72 VDC, 40 A maximum, typical 238 W and maximum 587 W. The datasheet's Table 4 gives the same four wattages at 220 to 240 V. The note on both: maximum measured at 40 C ambient with SR optics at 100 percent load with IMIX traffic; typical at 25 C with DACs at 50 percent load with IMIX traffic, excluding transceivers. The AC pair is the device's, since AC is the default build; the DC pair is carried under its own keys.

rear-layout.note: Rear photograph at 4.238 px/mm, checked against the guide's figures 17, 29 and 40: six fan modules numbered 0 to 5 from the left (the guide: "counting from left to right"), on a 44.0 mm pitch, the first at 55.1 mm; then two power supplies side by side at the right end, at 320.1 and 378.3 mm. The orange fan faces measure 40.7 mm wide and 40.8 mm high; the black supplies 55 mm by 41 mm. A chassis latch stands at the right end past the second supply. The fan and supply bays carry no chassis strip and no lamp on the chassis: the fan lamp is on the fan module (guide, QFX5130 Fan Module LED) and the three supply lamps are on the supply.

row-pitch.note: The SFP56-DD openings of one column measure 9.8 to 18.9 mm and 24.8 to 33.9 mm down in the photograph, centres 14.75 and 29.65, 14.9 apart; the registry's 15.0 for the single-port SFP shell is used. The uplinks measure centres 13.7 and 28.5 mm, 14.8 apart, used as 14.8. The registry gives no belly-to-belly pitch for SFP-DD or QSFP-DD, so these are the photograph's.

sfp-plus.note: Table 7: ports 56 and 57 take SFP+ (10 Gbps, link up) and nothing else. They are two single SFP cages one above the other at 37.25 mm from the left of the rear, each with a bicolour lamp above-left of its numeral (Table 11 describes one lamp for each). The latch tongues face each other, as on the front, so the upper cage is upright and the lower turned 180. The guide's note says the Finisar AOC SFP+ module needs pulling upwards to remove it; nothing is drawn for it.

sources.note: Juniper QFX5130 Switch Hardware Guide, published 2026-10-14, 234 pages (copyright HPE): the front and rear figures 16 to 19, the port panel figure 21 and the management panel figure 29, the network-port tables 7, 10 and 11, the chassis lamp table 14, the lamp figures 23, 30 to 32, the cooling tables 17 and 18 with figures 34 and 40, the power tables 20 and 27 and Table 31 (physical specifications). The QFX5130 Line of Switches Datasheet, 1000680-018-EN, July 2025, 9 pages (Juniper Networks): Tables 2 to 4 and the QFX5130-48C and QFX5130-48CM ordering information. Juniper's studio photographs from its image library of the QFX5130-48CM, front and rear (qfx5130-48cm-front-high.jpg, 2100 x 507 px, and qfx5130-48cm-rear-high.jpg, 2100 x 523 px), and of the QFX5130-48C (qfx5130-48c-front-high.jpg, 1500 x 210 px, qfx5130-48c-rear-high.jpg, 1500 x 203 px, and the left and front-with-top views). The guide's figures 18 and 19 are the same 48CM photographs at 3000 px. All of it is the maker's and public. The guide is copyrighted; the image library page states no terms of use for the photographs, so they are used only to read positions and none is copied. No Visio stencil or 3D model of the switch was available, and no mechanical drawing or 3D model was found on juniper.net either.

stack-orientation.note: The photograph shows the silver latch tongue at the foot of every upper cage and at the top of every lower one, so both lips face the band between the rows, and the key bumps are on the outer edges: the upper row upright and the lower one turned 180, which is also how TE's drawing draws a belly-to-belly pair (the lower row the upper turned over, key notches outward). It is the library's stack convention, read off the device.

variants.note: Datasheet ordering information: QFX5130-48C-AFO and -AFI (AC), QFX5130-48C-D-AFO and -D-AFI (DC), QFX5130-48C-CHAS (without supplies and fans), and the same five for the 48CM, with MACsec capability. The guide draws the 48C and the 48CM with the same front and the same rear, so the ten are configurations of this one device: QFX5130-48C-AFO, -AFI, -D-AFO, -D-AFI, -CHAS and QFX5130-48CM-AFO, -AFI, -D-AFO, -D-AFI, -CHAS. The datasheet describes the QFX5130-48C-D-AFI without the "redundant fans" words the others carry; the guide's Table 4 gives all four the same two supplies and six fan modules. NOT MODELLED: the MACsec software licence S-QFX5KC3-MACSEC-X, the software subscriptions, the grounding lug kit JNP-GL-2H6-1032-ST, and the QFX5130-1RU-4PRMK rack kit (below).

vents.note: Hexagonal holes in the sheet: a band along the bottom (about 34.8 to 40.8 mm down) the full width, two rows of cells above the cages, a field at the left edge and a column at the right edge. The top band is broken around the legends in the photograph and is drawn as the two rows of cells only, above the legend line. Pitched to the photograph (3.2 by 1.85 mm) and estimated.

bottom.empty: Not drawn by any source held. The guide's figures show no underside, and the photographs are of the front, rear, side and top in perspective only.

left.empty: Not drawn by any source held. The image library's left view is a perspective photograph and the mounting figures show the brackets on a side wall in perspective only, with no scale from which a hole could be placed.

placements.description: Table 14 - red steady: major hardware fault; yellow steady: minor system alarm; amber blinking: a major and a minor alarm; unlit: no alarm or halted
Table 14 - green steady: Junos OS Evolved is loaded and the system is operational; green blinking: it is loading or shutting down; unlit: powered off or halted
Table 14 - blue blinking: the beacon feature is enabled (request chassis beacon fpc 0 on); unlit: not enabled
Table 16 - the status lamp is amber steady at 1 Gbps and amber flashing at 100 Mbps, unlit at 10 Mbps or link down; the link activity lamp is green steady with a link and blinking with traffic

right.empty: Not drawn by any source held. The image library's right view is a perspective photograph and no figure shows the right wall flat.

top.empty: Not drawn by any source held. The guide gives no flat figure of the lid (its grounding figure shows the top in perspective only) and the image library's views of the top are perspective photographs with no scale.
